title: RankEvolve: Automating the Discovery of Retrieval Algorithms via LLM-Driven Evolution

mechanism.domainTask: Evolutionary discovery of lexical information-retrieval ranking algorithms
mechanism.populationDetail: K independently evolving islands each maintain a MAP-Elites grid over code complexity and edit-distance diversity, with periodic migration.
mechanism.archiveDetail: Each island preserves the best program per MAP-Elites cell defined by complexity and population-relative edit distance.
mechanism.replacementDetail: A candidate enters an empty descriptor cell or replaces its incumbent only when its optimization score is higher; top-fraction migration is a separate island-communication operation.
mechanism.generationDetail: The LLM edits one selected parent program through a SEARCH/REPLACE diff constrained to evolvable code regions.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Per-dataset Recall@100 and nDCG@10, combined scalar fitness, and latency are stored and supplied with the parent/reference programs; latency is visible but not optimized.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The selected mode chooses uniform island sampling, elite-archive sampling, or performance-proportional island sampling. Additionally T=4 best and S=4 random same-island programs are prompt references; they are not extra true parents. Mode probabilities are unspecified.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/RankEvolve Automating the Discovery of Retrieval Algorithms via LLM-Driven Evolution.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Current survey placements for islands/QD archive/replacement and prompt structure appear missing; RankEvolve is already covered for localized modification and fixed explore-exploit control. Its top-4 inspiration set is rank-selected context, not a set of true parents; validate the existing RankEvolve citation under Rank-Based parent selection. Exact p_e/p_x values and archive capacity eviction are not specified.
